title: BMW is taking on Tesla’s FSD with urban driver assist starting in 2027
summary:
BMW says that it will expand its navigation-guided, partially automated driving capabilities into urban environments starting in 2027, launching first in Germany with other markets to follow.
While driving in town, it can assist with changing lanes, making turns, yielding to other cars, and driving through roundabouts.
BMW, in particular, recently introduced its next-generation Neue Klasse platform, which includes a driver assist system partly powered by Qualcomm’s technology.
And with hands-free highway driving now widely available in many mass-market vehicles, the next frontier is a safe and capable city driving feature that rivals FSD.
BMW is entering risky territory with the adoption of a Level 2 driving feature.

title: iPhone Duo: Latest Buyer Wait Times
summary:
IPhone Duo order wait times averaged 89 days despite falling by a week, according to UBS Investment Bank data as of October 30.
The USB Evidence Lab tracker covers iPhone availability across more than 30 markets, and puts the iPhone Duo buyer wait time at nearly three months, even after the slight improvement.
By comparison, iPhone 18 Pro wait times averaged around five days, down three days from the previous week, while the Pro Max held steady at roughly 18 days.
iPhone Duo pre-orders slipped to late January within minutes on the device's October 16 launch, but most people who queued on launch day walked away with a new phone.

summary:

title: One of Google’s Android partners turned 1.3 million set-top boxes into a botnet
summary:
Google says one of its Android manufacturing partners secretly built a backdoor in 1.3 million devices and turned them into a botnet.
The infected devices were used without owners’ knowledge for “malicious activity,” like ad fraud, data exfiltration, and routing unauthorized network traffic.
Google claims the “backdoor and botnet were intentionally developed, deployed, and operated for financial gain,” saying:Videostrong monetized the backdoor by selling access to criminal affiliates and loading those affiliates’ malware modules onto infected devices.
These secondary modules were conducting ad-fraud; silently enrolling infected devices into residential proxy networks; and loading additional malware onto XCPE-compromised devices.
Google also says it made changes to its review process for device manufacturers after this incident.

title: The New York Times sues Brave web browser for AI scraping and bypassing paywalls
summary:
The New York Times and a group of other publications have filed lawsuits against the company that makes the Brave web browser over alleged unlawful scraping to train AI and also letting users bypass their paywalls, as reported by Reuters.
Brave has allegedly provided “stolen copyrighted content” to “many” AI companies including Anthropic, Perplexity, Mistral, xAI, and Cohere.
Brave also promotes “hundreds of top publishers” as being accessible through its “Paywall blocker” feature in its browser.
“Brave has never asked for the Publishers’ permission to access their websites, much less to copy the material and provide it to users or other AI companies,” the complaint says.
Also added a statement from the attorney who filed the lawsuit on behalf of those publications.

title: PsiQuantum Unveils Optical Circuit Switch Technology Built on Advanced, Low-Loss Silicon Photonics Platform — PsiQuantum
summary:
October 28, 2026PALO ALTO, Calif. – PsiQuantum today unveiled its Optical Circuit Switching (OCS) technology, demonstrating how the company’s advanced, low-loss silicon photonics platform can be applied to some of the most significant scaling challenges facing AI infrastructure.
AI systems are scaling faster than computing infrastructure, with increasingly large pools of compute placing enormous demands on the networks connecting them.
AI and quantum computing are complementary technologies: more efficient AI infrastructure can accelerate the development and operation of quantum systems, while some advances made for quantum computing can help remove bottlenecks in AI infrastructure.
As optics make AI infrastructure more efficient, stronger AI infrastructure can in turn support the design, control, and operation of increasingly capable quantum systems.
What we are demonstrating today is that this platform can deliver exceptional performance for optical circuit switching for AI computing."

title: AI delivers ‘zero financial payoff’ to most companies, Apollo economist says
summary:
In BriefAI hasn’t benefited the bottom line of any big corporations outside the tech industry, according to a note recently published by the chief economist at Apollo Global Management (the private equity giant that used to own TechCrunch).
Apollo’s Torsten Slok focuses on what he calls the S&P 493 — the S&P 500, minus Alphabet, Amazon, Apple, Meta, Microsoft, Nvidia, and Tesla — finding that profit margins and revenue per worker appear to be flat, with no evidence that AI is improving productivity.
“Despite massive investments and widespread hype around artificial intelligence, the technology has delivered zero financial payoff to corporate America outside of tech,” Slok said.
Is this simply a matter of non-tech companies lagging behind the tech giants?
Slok sounded skeptical, arguing that it will be tough for corporate America to “turn increasingly cheap intelligence into higher revenue growth and higher profit margins.”“AI may be a great calculator, but in business, intelligence is mostly judgment,” he wrote, later adding, “AI does not understand accountability, trust, culture, unwritten rules, ethical trade-offs or fairness, all of which shape reputational risk and ultimately drive revenue growth and profit margins.”Recent studies have also found that AI has yet to deliver significant productivity gains.

title: Thieves pilfer environment variables from Trigger AI workflow tool
summary:
If you're a customer of cloud-hosted AI workflow platform Trigger.dev, take heed, because your environment variables may have been exposed in a security incident disclosed on Sunday.
Trigger offered little explanation in its Sunday security incident report, noting that its investigation had identified “exposure across a subset of organizations” and that an attacker had gained unauthorized access to environment variables belonging to those organizations.
REG ADWe likely don't have to tell The Reg readers how important environment variables are in SaaS and cloud services like Trigger.
If compromised environment variables contain sensitive credentials, an attacker could basically end up with the keys to the kingdom, potentially gaining access to connected services and digital infrastructure.
Trigger has some fairly high-profile customers, with companies like fashion brand Emporio Armani, Pentagon-supporting AI acquisitions platform GovSignals, SaaS calendar platform Cal.com, and others all listed on the company’s site.

title: Over 370,000 Dreo Space Heaters Recalled After 17 Catch Fire
summary:
Dreo has recalled its DR-HSH015 space heater due to the risk of the unit catching fire.
DREO said it received 17 reports of space heaters igniting, three resulting in property damage and one in a burn injury to the hand.
The space heater was available from outlets including Home Depot, Best Buy, Kohl’s and Costco, as late as October 2026.
Owners should stop using the recalled space heaters immediately, disconnect them from power, destroy them by cutting off the power cable and contact the company for a free replacement.
Space heaters are a popular way to heat cold rooms, and CNET’s own tests found that properly functioning units can help owners reduce their energy bills over winter.

title: Microsoft AI chief says AI is not conscious and we should keep it that way
summary:
Mustafa Suleyman said in a lengthy X post on Sunday that AI models currently don't have consciousness and that developers should keep it that way.
"If consciousness started to emerge in training, I would call for everyone to stop AI development until we could design out those properties."
If any evidence were to emerge that AI models were conscious, Suleyman said it must be disclosed to the general public immediately so we can decide our next steps as a society.
Conversations around whether AI models could one day become conscious are picking up steam in the tech world.
Google DeepMind published research papers this year about AI consciousness and how ascribing that characteristic could present challenges.
